subject: general
question: Accumulation of which substance in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lactic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lactic acid** accumulates in muscles during intense exercise or sudden activity.
 
• This happens because of **anaerobic respiration**, where glucose is broken down without oxygen to produce energy.
 
• The buildup of **lactic acid** leads to a condition known as **muscle acidosis**, causing cramps and fatigue.
 
• This process is typically a temporary response to high-intensity exercise.
 
• The body usually clears out lactic acid through the bloodstream once the activity level decreases and oxygen becomes available.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sucrose**__

 __
 
• **Sucrose** is a common sugar found in many plants and is used as a sweetener in foods and beverages.
 
• It does not accumulate in muscles nor cause cramps during physical activity.
 
 
 
• **Glucose**__
 __
 
• **Glucose** is the primary source of energy for the body's cells.
 
• During exercise, glucose is broken down to produce energy, but it does not directly cause cramps.
 
 
 
• **Pyruvic acid**__
 
 
• **Pyruvic acid** is an intermediate product in the breakdown of glucose during cellular respiration.
 
• It does not accumulate in muscles during exercise; instead, it is converted to lactic acid under anaerobic conditions.
